set.st: July 1939: the three young Belote boys dug up a drain tile holding $1,880 in $5/$10/$20 gold (1882-1902) on the farm 4-4½ mi NW-W of Bronson, on the Matteson-Bronson township line; days later Frank Belote kicked up an iron pipe with $1,120 in gold 12 ft away. A second tile, plugged with concrete at both ends, which the boys had used as a toy smokestack, was never found again. Owner Kregger ordered no more digging and evicted the Belotes. The original owner, who died in 1904, was said to have buried several lots of gold; a buried safe was dug up on the farm 25+ years before 1939, and the owner had plowed up a pipe of gold the year before the tile find. Pin is on the farmsteads at the township line, not the spot itself. In Jan 1941 Judge Renshaw split the $3,000 found in 1939 half to the finders and half to the heirs of the former owners, who buried it before 1921. The AP account puts the $1,100 in a tin can under the front porch and adds a third cache of $100. The local papers add: it was the old Canaris 'Canary' Phillips farm (he died c.1906; the papers also give 1904 and 1921), bought by Kregger from a Chicago man. The tile lay barely under the surface in an open field near a clothes-line standard; a pipe plowed up the year before had been tossed in a fence corner; a small safe of money was unearthed soon after Phillips's death. The Free Press said Phillips 'banked most of his solid cash in secret places of burial about his farm'. The gold was legally the Phillips estate's, hence the 1941 split.
set.pl: Old Canaris Phillips farm on the Matteson-Bronson township line, about 4-4½ mi NW-W of Bronson: C. N. Phillips 40 (E strip of S½ sec. 32 T6S R8W, Matteson Twp, 1915 atlas) and the estate strip in N sec. 5 T7S R8W just south. The Battle Creek Enquirer's "2 mi east" (17 Jul) is the error; its 18 Jul '4 mi NW' and the Gazette's '4½ mi W' agree.
pinev: 1915 Branch atlas Matteson plate: C. N. Phillips 40, easternmost N-S strip of S½ sec 32 T6S R8W on the township line; the Bronson plate shows the estate strip continuing across N sec 5. 1900 census puts the widow in Matteson Twp.

On 2017 Michigan 1 m lidar two farmyard pads sit on the township-line road: one N of the road at about 41.8981,-85.2563 (sec 32, just W of the strip) and one S of it at about 41.8971,-85.2551 (N end of the sec 5 strip). No 1938 aerial read; the ring covers both yards.
set.t: Two caches were found in the house yard and field; a second concrete-plugged tile, reported in two independent local papers, is unaccounted for. Check both farmyards on the township line on the 1938-40 aerial. Access: private farm: permission.
set.tovw: Lead grade C (treasure thread): the $3,000 recovered is accounted for and split in 1941; a missing plugged tile is in two independent local papers
